published_statement: Eq.(22)/(5.22): Delta <= (3/4) sqrt(3/pi) v_b/alpha^2 [Planck units]; eq.(23) 'as an example, if we let alpha = 1/10, then Delta <= 10^2 v_b L_Planck ... Thus, unless v_b is extremely large, the wall thickness cannot be much above the Planck scale.' Eq.(28) E = -(1/12) v_b^2 (R^2/Delta + Delta/12); with R = 100 m and eq.(23): eq.(29) 'E <= -6.2x10^70 v_b L_Planck ~ -6.2x10^65 v_b grams'; eq.(31) 'E <= -3x10^20 M_galaxy v_b ... roughly ten orders of magnitude greater than the total mass of the entire visible universe.' Delta = 1 m, R = 100 m: 'on the order of a quarter of a solar mass'. Summary: 'a bubble with a radius the size of one electron Compton wavelength would require a negative energy of the order E ~ -400 M_sun.' Abstract: 'bubble wall thickness is on the order of only a few hundred Planck lengths'.
published_hypotheses: H1 free, massless scalar field in 4D; Ford-Roman 1995 QI with Lorentzian sampling, eq.(9): (tau0/pi) Int <T_uv u^u u^v>/(tau^2+tau0^2) >= -3/(32 pi^2 tau0^4) (minimal coupling implicit); massive scalar stated 'even more restrictive', EM field 'larger by a factor of sqrt2' (stated, not derived)

H2 the FLAT-space QI applied directly to the curved Alcubierre metric, justified by the Ford-Roman 1996 argument that it holds when the sampling time is <= the smallest local curvature radius; the exact curved treatment 'would be exceptionally difficult' (p.2)

H3 sampling time t0 = alpha * r_min, r_min = 2 Delta/(sqrt3 v_b) from the largest orthonormal Riemann component |R_tyty| (eq.18-20), with 0 < alpha << 1 UNSPECIFIED; alpha = 1/10 is 'an example' (eq.23)
H4 v_s(t) ~ v_b constant over the sampling interval (sampling time << velocity-change time)
H5 observer = Alcubierre's Eulerian geodesic (u_mu = (-1,0,0,0)) sampled at the bubble equator crossing, geodesic approximated as x(t) ~ f(rho) v_b t (eq.11)
H6 Delta/rho ~ v_b t0/rho << 1 (eq.21) to drop the (1-f) term
H7 order-of-magnitude: piecewise-linear shape function (eq.4) stands for any shape via the leading Taylor term f'(rho) ~ 1/Delta (eq.13)
H8 semiclassical identification <T_uv u^u u^v> = G_00/8pi (eq.8): the quantum field alone sources the Alcubierre geometry
H9 energy figure: constant-velocity bubble, R = 100 m, Delta saturating eq.(23), energy = integral of Eulerian-measured density over the t=0 slice (eq.25)
H10 Alcubierre geometry (metric eq.1), 4D, G = c = hbar = 1

rederivation.outcome: Every closed-form step re-derived and agrees: eq.(10) from (8)+(9); eq.(12)/(15) r_s^2 = v^2(1-f)^2(t^2+beta^2); eq.(14); eq.(16) contour integral = pi/(t0 beta (t0+beta)); eq.(17); eq.(19) r_min = 2Delta/(sqrt3 v_b); eq.(22) coefficient = 3sqrt3/(4sqrtpi) = (3/4)sqrt(3/pi) = 0.7329 (the arXiv text layer's '3/4 sqrt3 pi' is the layout of sqrt(3/pi), confirmed by the algebra and by the thesis eq.5.22), alpha = 1/10 -> 73.3 v_b L_P ('10^2'); angular integral 8pi/3 -> -v^2/12 (eq.26); radial integral R^2/Delta + Delta/12 (eq.28). Numbers: R = 100 m -> E = 6.94e62 kg = 6.94e65 g (paper 6.2e65 g, x0.89) = 3.47e20 x (2e45 g) (paper 3e20); ten-orders claim: 9.67 orders vs baryons. DISCREPANCIES recorded, not refutations: (a) intermediate '6.2e70 v_b L_P' is 1.94x the computed 3.19e70 L_P, compensated by a 1e-5 g/L_P conversion so the gram figure agrees; (b) 'E ~ -400 M_sun' for R = lambda_C is not reproduced: own formula gives -2.06e5 M_sun (x514), independently matched by Van Den Broeck eq.(9) scaled by R^2 (2.07e5); (c) Delta = 1 m, R = 100 m gives 0.56 M_sun vs 'on the order of a quarter' (x2.2). Van Den Broeck eq.(9) (6.3e29 kg) reproduced by the 1/12 formula to <1%, confirming the formula and constants. Exit 0.

later_literature.ref: Van Den Broeck, 'A warp drive with more reasonable total energy requirements', CQG 16 (1999) 3973, arXiv gr-qc/9905084
later_literature.what: Keeps P&F's wall bound Delta <= 10^2 v_s L_P (his eq.6) and their eq.(28), but a pocket geometry B(r_s) with a 3e-15 m outer bubble and 200 m inner diameter needs only a few solar masses (E_IV ~ -6.3e29 kg, E_II- ~ -1.4e30 kg, E_II+ ~ +4.9e30 kg) and satisfies the flat-space QI for Eulerian observers. The 1e62 kg energy conclusion is specific to the Alcubierre geometry at R = 100 m, not to warp geometries generally; the wall bound and Planck-scale structure survive ('structure with sizes only a few orders of magnitude above the Planck scale; this seems to be generic'). Also restates P&F's figure as E ~ -6.2e62 v_s kg.

later_literature.ref: Kontou & Olum, 'Quantum inequality in spacetimes with small curvature', PRD 91 (2015) 104005, arXiv 1410.0665
later_literature.what: Proves (from Fewster & Smith's absolute QEI, gr-qc/0702056) that for a massless minimally coupled scalar on a timelike geodesic the flat-space QI holds with first-order corrections in the Ricci tensor and its derivatives, small when R_max t0^2, R''_max t0^4, R'''_max t0^5 << 1; 'The present paper explicitly confirms this claim [Ford-Roman: flat-space QIs apply in curved spacetime at small sampling times]' and cites P&F as ref [7]. Caveats it adds: curvature must be small over the whole causal diamond of the sampled segment, and there are renormalization ambiguities a, b. For the P&F setting the leading correction ~ R_max t0^2 = alpha^2 = 0.01 (computed; ~0.7% of the Gaussian flat term) -- order-of-magnitude estimate, since Kontou-Olum's bound uses Ricci and Gaussian sampling.

later_literature.ref: Bobrick & Martire, 'Introducing Physical Warp Drives', CQG 38 (2021) 105009, arXiv 2102.06824
later_literature.what: Cites P&F as the reason the Alcubierre drive is unphysical (p.2) and restates their QI (eq.4). Narrows the ENERGY conclusion to the Alcubierre shape: the variational optimum f = min(r0/r,1) lowers |E| by ~3x (App. A.3, their eq. A.7 reproduces P&F's -(v^2/12) Int r^2 f'^2 dr, i.e. P&F eq.26), and flattening along x by alpha_X lowers E proportionally, allowing superluminal solutions that satisfy the P&F-form QI -- which they say 'more likely probe the limits of applicability of the quantum inequalities' and which still violate ANEC (sec.4.2). Also contests Van Den Broeck: argues (App. A.2) his metric is Alcubierre in new coordinates with region-1 energy scaling as B(0)^2, so his small region-1 energy may be an underestimate. Does not dispute the wall-thickness bound for the spherical Alcubierre bubble.

later_literature.ref: Pfenning, PhD thesis 'Quantum inequality restrictions on negative energy densities in curved spacetimes' (Tufts 1998), arXiv gr-qc/9805037, ch.5
later_literature.what: Same authors' text verbatim (eqs 5.1-5.30), with eq.(5.22) Delta <= (3/4) sqrt(3/pi) v_b/alpha^2, and the claim that the flat-space application is known to be valid from the thesis's own short-sampling expansion (sec.3.3) -- which is derived for STATIC spacetimes, while Alcubierre is not static. Repeats the 6.2e70 L_P and -400 M_sun figures (so the discrepancies are not arXiv-version artefacts).

lacked_data: What the authors lacked in 1997, and whether having it changes the conclusion. (1) A proven curved-spacetime QI for a NON-static metric: they said the exact treatment 'would be exceptionally difficult' and used the flat QI at short sampling (H2). Supplied later: Fewster & Smith (2008) and Kontou & Olum (1410.0665, READ) prove the flat form plus first-order Ricci corrections, small when t0 is below curvature radii; for P&F's choice t0 = alpha r_min the leading correction scales as alpha^2 (computed 0.01 at alpha = 0.1). Evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result: the one gap the authors named was later closed in their favour to first order. (2) Cosmological masses (Milky Way ~0.8-1.5e12 M_sun, observable-universe baryons 1.5e53 kg): the moved values shift E/M_gal within 2.3e20-4.4e20 and leave 'roughly ten orders' at 9.7 (baryons) -- no change. (3) Later constructions, not data: Van Den Broeck 1999 (READ) shows the ~1e62 kg total energy is geometry-specific (few solar masses in a pocket geometry that still satisfies the QI); non-minimal coupling (0708.2450, named) has no state-independent QEI. These narrow the scope (Alcubierre geometry; minimally coupled scalar or EM field) rather than reversing the wall-thickness conclusion, which Van Den Broeck keeps. (4) Not lacking data but arithmetic: two printed figures do not follow from the paper's own formulas (6.2e70 L_P, x1.94; -400 M_sun, x514 low) -- discrepancies, recorded; the qualitative conclusions they illustrate stand. Net: no datum the authors lacked moves their conclusion within H1-H10; later work narrows the class it applies to. Added in this continuation: Bobrick & Martire 2102.06824 (READ) is a later construction, not a datum; it narrows the total-energy figure to the Alcubierre shape (x3 by shape optimisation, more by flattening) and leaves the timelike-QI wall bound for the spherical Alcubierre bubble untouched.
grade_evidence: The source's derivation stands as published: every closed-form step (eqs 10, 12, 14-17, 19, 22, 26, 28) is re-derived symbolically and agrees; the headline R = 100 m energy is reproduced to 11% in grams (6.94e65 g vs 6.2e65 g) and 3.47e20 vs 3e20 M_galaxy; no moved datum (CODATA 2022, Milky Way mass, Planck-2018 baryon mass) changes a conclusion; the one gap the authors named (flat QI on a curved metric) was later confirmed to first order by Kontou & Olum 1410.0665 (READ). It is NARROWED for three reasons. (i) The tree's use drops hypotheses the result needs: alpha (certify.py:25, 394; nullbound.py:157-159, 211), the massless minimally coupled scalar broadened to 'free quantum field' (non-minimal coupling has no state-independent QEI, per the tree's own overturn.py:285-289), and R = 100 m and v_b on the energy figure (anec.py:66, index3.py:386). (ii) overturn.py:59-61 and 280-283 attribute to P&F more than they state: 'every known QI' and 'sub-Planckian', where P&F bound the wall at a few hundred Planck lengths. (iii) Later work (Van Den Broeck gr-qc/9905084, READ) confirms the wall bound but limits the total-energy conclusion to the Alcubierre geometry. Recorded as a discrepancy, not a refutation: the -400 M_sun figure the tree keeps (certify.py:38-40) is 514x below the paper's own formula (2.06e5 M_sun, matched independently by scaling Van Den Broeck eq.9). Not WRONG: no counterexample to the inequality or the bound is shown here. Later reading added (2026-09-26): Bobrick & Martire 2102.06824 (READ) further narrows the energy conclusion to the spherical Alcubierre shape and does not touch the wall-thickness bound; grade unchanged.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restates the bound as Delta <= 0.733 v_b/alpha^2 L_P (10^2 at alpha = 1/10), names the massless minimally coupled scalar or EM field and the Alcubierre geometry at R = 100 m, removes 'sub-Planckian ... Pfenning-Ford's conclusion' and 'every known QI' from the P&F attribution, and drops or corrects the -400 M_sun figure. To WRONG: a computed counterexample, meaning a minimally coupled free scalar state on an Alcubierre wall that satisfies the curved-spacetime QEI (Fewster-Smith / Kontou-Olum form, including second-order curvature terms) with Delta much larger than 0.733 v_b/alpha^2 L_P at small alpha. To DATA-DEPENDENT: none foreseeable, since the bound contains no measured input apart from hbar, G and c. To OPEN: none, because the source was READ in full.
